Harbour bridge reopens after a two-year refit

Traffic crossed the span at dawn for the first time since the deck was lifted.

The first vehicles rolled over the harbour bridge shortly after five, ending a closure that had rerouted the whole eastern side of the city onto the tunnel and the two remaining ferries. Engineers had warned from the start that the deck replacement could not be staged in halves, and so the span came down to bare trusses for most of a winter.

The refit replaced every one of the original deck panels, along with the hangers that carry them, and added a separated lane on the seaward side for cyclists and pedestrians who had shared a metre of painted asphalt with freight since the bridge opened.

Costs ran over, as the inquiry into the contract had expected them to, and the final figure will not be published until the audit closes in the spring. The operator says the deck should now last forty years without a comparable closure.

For the ferry crews who carried the overflow, the reopening is the end of a long run of extra sailings. Two of the three relief boats go back on charter at the end of the month, and the night crossing that was added at the start of the closure will be kept through the winter before it is reviewed.

Commuters queuing on the approach before dawn said the difference was immediate. The tunnel, which had absorbed most of the diverted traffic, was clear by seven for the first morning anyone on the ramp could remember.
